facts.note: His revolt began in 73 BC when, along with about 70 other gladiators, he escaped a gladiatorial school near Capua. / Spartacus was trained at the gladiatorial school (ludus) near Capua belonging to Lentulus Batiatus.
Plutarch describes him as "a Thracian of Nomadic stock."
Ultimately, Marcus Licinius Crassus was tasked with suppressing the revolt. … Spartacus's forces were defeated in 71 BC.
6,000 captured rebels were crucified along the Appian Way.

question.hintNote: Marx called Spartacus "the most splendid fellow in the whole of ancient history."
